literal: To the scriptures of the righteous and to virtue, as the foundation, stood the king's sceptre.
translation: The sceptre of a just king stands as the very foundation for both the sacred scriptures of the wise and the virtue of the world.
modern: அறிஞர்களின் நூல்களுக்கும் அறத்திற்கும் அடிப்படையாக விளங்குவது மன்னனின் செங்கோல் ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of just governance in preserving society. The poet states that the sceptre of the king ('மன்னவன் கோல்') stands ('நின்றது') as the ultimate foundation ('ஆதியாய்') for both the sacred scriptures of the wise ('அந்தணர் நூற்கும்') and the practice of virtue ('அறத்திற்கும்') in the land. Without a just ruler to maintain order and protect the people, neither spiritual wisdom nor moral conduct can survive or flourish. Thus, the rule of law is the prerequisite for all higher human pursuits.
